newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki stock, derivatives markets to merge.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki stock, derivatives markets to merge.

text.p: The Helsinki Stock Exchange and Finnish derivatives exchange SOM Oy said on Tuesday they planned to merge, upping the pace of consolidation in Nordic securities markets following a Swedish-Danish link set last month.

The deal creates a new company called HEX Oy by year-end and follows a tie-up between Denmark's stock and futures and options exchanges last September and a plan last month from the Copenhagen and Stockholm bourses to combine trading systems.

The exchanges said the merger, aimed at enhancing Finnish capital markets, would simplify their structure and boost cooperation and competitiveness internationally. Most analysts welcomed the merger's cost-cutting potential.

Finnish stock exchange volumes have risen sharply recently, but the exchange clearly remains the smallest of the four main Nordic markets, with about one-tenth of the area's total 207 billion ECU turnover in the 12 months to May.
Although the bourses said the merger would strengthen their position as a potential international partner, they said they were not now discussing a Nordic link-up.

"The future is the future, and we believe that with what we have now, we will be a strong partner," Juha Korhonen, chairman of SOM Oy told a news conference. "(But) at this time, we are not engaged in any negotiations in any direction."

If the deal goes as planned, banking group Merita will be the largest owner of the new exchange with 29.8 percent, and Swedish futures and options exchange OM Gruppen OMFKf.ST the second largest with 15.7 percent, they said.
Voting power is restricted to 1/20 of total votes.

"Domestic capital markets are undergoing a period of unprecedented change. Traditional stock exchange structures and national markets will be subjected to hard international competition," the exchanges said in a statement.

European economic and monetary union (EMU) would encourage cross-border trade between member countries, but remote membership and cooperation also offered new opportunities for smaller markets, they said.
"Their (the exchanges') challenge is to create liquidity and client value, and we think this solution gives chances for this," said an OM Gruppen spokesman in Stockholm.

Bourse CEO Juhani Erma will be president and chief executive officer of HEX Oy and Asko Schrey, Managing Director of SOM, will be appointed chief operating officer and deputy chief executive officer, the exchanges said.
Last year, combined turnover of the merging exchanges was 97 million markka ($18.7 million), with profits of 34 million markka.
The exchanges said SOM's products can be traded in Stockholm and at the market operated by OM's London-based exchange, OMLX, and corresponding OM products can be traded in Finland.
But it was not yet clear if the bourse's all-share HEX or the widely-used derivatives exchange's FOX would be the new exchange's benchmark.
A bourse spokeswoman said she believed the partners had not yet discussed that question.
